title: She’s survived four gerrymanders and a car crash. Can her luck hold?
description: Rep. Marcy Kaptur (D-Ohio), 80, has been unbeatable, even as her district gets redrawn again and again.

title: Most Michigan voters disapprove of Trump’s tariffs on Canada, poll shows
description: Among the state’s independents, who could determine the outcome of several key midterm races, 68 percent disapprove of Trump's levies on Canadian products.

title: Congress is getting older, and Americans aren’t happy
description: This was a significant week in the debate about aging politicians.

title: Why Democrats are starting to feel bullish about a midterm wave
description: Democrats say the Iran war, high prices and President Donald Trump's sinking popularity give them a real chance of congressional majorities.

title: White House withdraws nomination of Lance Schroyer to lead ICE
description: President Trump's nominee to lead U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement was former Oklahoma state trooper Lance Schroyer. Three months after tapping him for the job, his name is being withdrawn.

title: Google is helping write AI chatbot safety laws — while pushing for loopholes
description: As states push to regulate chatbots, tech companies are trying to write safety rules in ways that exempt some of their key products.

title: Republican 'cavalry' arrives with a Trump-backed $150 million ad blitz in key races
description: To counter a difficult political environment, two Trump-aligned super PACs have reserved more than $150 million in ads — primarily in deep red House and Senate races that have now become competitive.

title: A DHS email raises new questions about the Trump administration's election plans
description: A heavily redacted email from last year, reported first by NPR, reveals that DHS personnel shared a list of jurisdictions that offer election materials in non-English languages. It's unclear why.

title: Some GOP candidates are still making election fraud claims. Voters want to move on
description: President Trump and some Republican battleground candidates are still embracing false claims about widespread election fraud in 2020, even as many GOP voters want them to move on.

title: Republican candidate in Florida runs ads criticizing Trump's immigration enforcement
description: In a rare move, a House Republican running in a competitive race in South Florida is publicly breaking with President Trump. Maria Elvira Salazar represents a majority Hispanic district.

title: Texas Republican candidate under fire for comment about university students of color
description: A Texas Republican's complaint that too many people of color were in a video of the crowd at a University of Texas football game set off condemnations.

title: Trump's week of setbacks: The president's priorities get rare pushback
description: President Trump's agenda has run into rare institutional pushback on a variety of issues from mail-in voting to the Federal Reserve.

title: What do Trump's supporters think of the political pushback he's faced
description: NPR's Michel Martin speaks with Will Sommer of The Bulwark about the pushback President Trump has faced at home and abroad on some of his policies and initiatives.

title: It's illegal for armed federal officers to be at polls. Lawsuits seek to ensure that
description: The latest lawsuit, first reported by NPR, argues the Trump administration's repeated suggestions that federal officers could be at polling sites is a form of illegal voter intimidation.

title: RFK Jr. says Americans worried about vaccines have a ‘friend at the White House’
description: Since being confirmed as health secretary, Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has made clear he wants to overhaul the nation’s immunization system.

title: Senator blocks bill meant to lower electricity prices linked to data centers
description: Sen. Martin Heinrich (D-New Mexico) halted passage of a proposal that had passed the House by an overwhelming margin.

title: What to know about the Kennedy Center closing under Trump
description: His allies have warned that it could be permanent if his name is not added to the iconic arts venue.

title: U.S. will let Iranian leaders attend U.N. General Assembly in New York
description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian is scheduled to address the annual gathering of world leaders on Wednesday.

title: Democrats seize on House GOP’s decision to leave town early
description: The Republican-led chamber has no more workdays scheduled in Washington before the November midterms.

title: Mike Pence says he has ‘no plans’ to run for president in 2028
description: Mike Pence says he has no plans to run for president in 2028.

title: Why Karl Rove, a father of the modern Texas GOP, is voting for a Democrat
description: How Texas Republicans abandoned their immigrant-welcoming tradition.

title: The Pollwatcher: Inside The Washington Post-Schar School poll on Michigan
description: Plus: AI layoff fears and measles vaccine trust.

title: Democrats demand to know where Venezuelan oil revenue is going
description: The Trump administration seized control of Venezuelan oil after capturing President Nicolás Maduro in January.

title: As warnings mount, Democrats eyeing the presidency wake up to AI fears
description: Their plans are heavier on rhetoric than specifics so far. But it’s a shift for many in the party who have been slow to address the fast-changing technology.

title: We polled Michigan’s Senate race. There’s good and bad news for Democrats.
description: A Post-Schar School finds 53 percent of Michigan’s likely voters say they want Democrats to control the Senate, but 48 percent support Democrat Abdul El-Sayed in the Senate race.

title: Trump won by latching on to popular issues. He’s doing the opposite on AI.
description: It's been stunning to see this president so firmly position himself on the unpopular side of the debate around AI and data centers.

title: Trump emphasizes crime in midterm push in North Carolina
description: The president made violent crime the central issue in his first large-scale outdoor rally this year and cites the GOP’s 1988 “Willie Horton” attack ad on Democratic nominee Michael S. Dukakis.

title: House passes bill attempting to lower data center costs
description: The bill, one of Congress’s first efforts to rein in the unpopular facilities, was approved with overwhelming bipartisan support but is unlikely to lower prices immediately.

title: On the Kennedy Center’s last day, silence and sadness
description: An eerie silence, empty halls and security guards marked the end, at least for now, of a once-vibrant public space.

title: Afghan terrorist gets 20 years for role in deadly 2021 attack at Kabul airport
description: Thirteen American troops and about 170 Afghans were killed in a suicide bombing at the airport’s Abbey Gate as the U.S. left Afghanistan.

title: Iowa’s Republican Senate candidate not attending JD Vance event
description: A spokesperson for Rep. Ashley Hinson, who is campaigning on bipartisanship, cited previously scheduled events but declined to say what they are.

title: Trump’s arch will harm historic sites but must proceed, federal officials say
description: National Park Service officials acknowledge that President Donald Trump’s planned arch would harm dozens of historic sites but say it must move forward anyway.

title: Senate Republicans manage to advance farm bill with McConnell’s return
description: The measure still faces significant challenges as Democrats demand changes to SNAP provisions.

title: Susie Wiles, Trump’s chief of staff, says she is cancer-free
description: Wiles had continued working at the White House while undergoing treatment.

title: Sen. Cassidy says measles surge will be administration’s ‘terrible legacy’
description: Under questioning by Sen. Bill Cassidy (R-Louisiana), Trump’s surgeon general pick Nicole Saphier called a combined vaccine “our greatest tool for combating measles infections.”

title: House holds billionaire Leon Black in contempt over Epstein probe subpoena
description: Billionaire Leon Black held contempt over Epstein investigation subpoena; Black denies any wrongdoing or any knowledge of Epstein's behavior.

title: How to argue about regulating AI
description: Will regulation let China get ahead, or save us from doomsday?

title: The House is heading home ahead of the midterms even earlier than planned
description: A move to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth will now probably be considered after the November elections.

title: In leaked recording, Nebraska Senate candidate criticizes some Trump voters
description: Dan Osborn has carefully sought to maintain an independent profile to attract crossover voters of both parties in the typically red state.

title: Former congressman Sander Levin endorses El-Sayed for U.S. Senate in Michigan
description: In a statement, Levin said he was aligned with El-Sayed on climate change, trade, health care and other issues despite his “significant disagreement” with El-Sayed’s views on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

title: The Democratic fundraising machine under GOP investigation is fighting back
description: A law firm representing ActBlue reviewed its donation history and met with congressional investigators to present its evidence that the Democratic fundraising platform did not mislead Congress.

title: Iranian strikes have damaged hundreds of structures at U.S. bases, watchdog says
description: The report by the Pentagon's inspector general also detailed the extent of munitions shortfalls in the first comprehensive public accounting of the cost and military impact of the war with Iran.

title: Spanberger is bullish about Virginia House races even without a favorable map
description: An unusual fundraising alliance among Virginia Democrats highlights how the state can still help determine balance of power in the House this fall even though redistricting efforts were nullified by a court ruling.
